tasks.short: Interview the client, gather educational and medical records, consult other professionals, write up the interview, analyze everything to assess abilities, needs and eligibility, complete the assessment report, and send it to the client.

steps.what: Rehabilitation counselor explains the recording, asks the client's consent and starts it
Rehabilitation counselor interviews the client about abilities, needs and goals
Client signs the consent form for releasing school and medical records in the case system
Rehabilitation counselor prepares requests for educational and medical records with the client's consent form
Rehabilitation counselor checks each request: which records, the client's signed consent and the school or doctor it goes to
Rehabilitation counselor sends the checked requests from the case system and receives the records
Rehabilitation counselor consults other professionals about the client
Rehabilitation counselor writes up the interview notes

loop.input: The recording of the intake interview, made with the client's consent.
loop.output: Draft interview notes in the case system's format.
loop.check: A validator flags every statement on risk (suicide, violence, abuse) and every quote not found in the transcript. The counselor reads the full draft against the transcript, checks that each statement says what the client said and nothing more, corrects it and approves.
loop.stop: One draft per interview; if the counselor rejects it, they write the notes themselves.
loop.why_not_simpler: Dictation still leaves the counselor to compose the notes; a draft from the recording saves composing.

steps.what: Rehabilitation counselor analyzes the information to assess the client's abilities, needs and eligibility for services
Rehabilitation counselor completes and signs the assessment report
Rehabilitation counselor checks the final assessment report: the assessment, the client data the template filled in and the client's address
Rehabilitation counselor sends the checked assessment report to the client

tasks.design: With the client's consent, the intake interview is recorded and a bounded step drafts the notes in the case system ({OTHER}); a validator flags every risk statement and every quote not in the transcript, and the counselor reads and corrects the whole draft. Records from schools and doctors are requested through a consent form in the case system. The report template fills in client data. Assessing abilities, needs and eligibility stays with the counselor: no software scores eligibility. Once signed, the report goes to the client.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were written from memory after the talk and records chased by e-mail and phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech tools draft case notes from recorded talks in Dutch care and social work.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can invent statements, and clients may say less when recorded.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what a client can do that no record shows.
tasks.altitude: The counselor checks drafted notes instead of writing them from memory.

reach.learn: Whether assessments arrive within the deadline.

evidence.claim: Attendi turns spoken notes into a SOEP report or letter in the care record, used by 300+ care organisations.
Somerset Council's Magic Notes pilot with 20 staff reported about 11 hours a week saved per practitioner, self-reported.
UK social workers found invented suicidal ideation in AI-drafted notes.
AI used to decide eligibility for public assistance and services is high-risk under Annex III 5(a); here no software assesses eligibility.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to the report sent; the decision on services is outside.
Input contract: recordings only with the client's consent; records released with consent; fallback is notes from memory and e-mail requests.

Interviewing, consulting, assessing and the checks before each send do not change. About 70% of clients consent to recording; s4 is priced at that share. The client's consent signature (s2a) is about what a paper form took. s7 keeps 20 for printing or sending the report.
A DPIA and works council consent come before any recording.
research_questions: Do clients say less when the talk is recorded?

already_counted.description: Rehabilitation counselor reads and corrects the drafted notes.

incremental.description: No new work: asking consent is shown as step s0.

approvals.approved_version: The signed assessment report exactly as checked by the counselor in s6b, sent once to the client at the checked address; any change needs a new check and signature.

Each record request with the records asked for and the client's signed consent exactly as checked by the counselor in s2b, sent once from the case system to the named school or doctor; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of clients decline recording, so s4 keeps 65, and schools and doctors still need chasing by phone, so s2 keeps 80 (13.5); high: 70% consent and requests through the case system (18.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet the client to review progress, ask the employer or training provider how it goes, record progress notes, update goals and hours, check the progress report, and send it to the funding agency.

steps.what: Rehabilitation counselor meets the client to review progress against goals
Employer or training provider fills the short form on attendance and progress
Rehabilitation counselor phones the employer or training provider about progress
Rehabilitation counselor records progress notes in the case file
Rehabilitation counselor monitors goals and hours in a spreadsheet
Rehabilitation counselor checks the final progress report: notes per goal, hours and attendance against the case file and the employer's form
Rehabilitation counselor submits the checked progress report to the funding agency's portal

tasks.design: Before the call, the employer or training provider gets a short form on attendance and progress, so the call covers problems only. After a contact, the counselor speaks a short summary and a bounded step drafts notes per goal in the case system ({OTHER}); a validator flags risk statements and goals without a note, and the counselor corrects and approves. Goals and hours show on a case dashboard instead of a spreadsheet. Once checked, the progress report goes to the funding agency ({GOV_PORTAL}). Talks with the client stay with the counselor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed after each contact and goals tracked in separate spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech tools draft notes in Dutch care records; case systems show goal status.
tasks.still_hard: Progress in confidence or health is hard to put in a form.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a client is losing heart before they miss a day.
tasks.altitude: The counselor checks drafted notes and dashboards instead of typing and tallying.

evidence.claim: Attendi turns spoken notes into a SOEP report or letter in the care record.
Health data are special category data; a DPIA comes first.

assumptions: Boundary: from the reintegration plan to the report submitted; decisions by the funding agency are outside.
Input contract: plan goals in the case system; employer form answers; fallback is phone calls and typing.

Employers fill the short form (s1b) in place of part of the call; no added employer time. Hours on the dashboard come from the employer's form on actual attendance. s6 keeps 10 for the submission itself.
Talks with the client do not change.
s3 is part of keeping case files, which sibling task 21-1015.00:9202 covers; its saving is counted there, so s3 keeps its full time here.
research_questions: Do progress reports reach the funding agency on time more often?

already_counted.description: Rehabilitation counselor reads and corrects the drafted notes.

incremental.description: Rehabilitation counselor follows up employers who do not fill the form.

approvals.approved_version: The progress report with notes per goal, hours and attendance exactly as checked by the counselor in s5, submitted once to the funding agency's portal for that client and period; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of employers skip the form, so s2 keeps 85 and hours are still typed, so s4 keeps 50 (13.2); high: forms and dashboard as designed (18.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit schools and community groups, keep in touch by e-mail and phone, keep the list of referral sources, write updates on services, and send them to referral sources.

steps.what: Rehabilitation counselor visits schools and community groups to develop relationships
Rehabilitation counselor keeps in touch with referral sources by e-mail and phone
Rehabilitation counselor keeps the list of community referral sources
Rehabilitation counselor writes an update on services for referral sources
Rehabilitation counselor checks the final service update: services, dates and contacts, and the mailing list
Rehabilitation counselor sends the checked update from the CRM to the referral sources' mailing list

tasks.design: Referral sources sit in a shared social map in the CRM ({CRM}) that the team keeps together, instead of each counselor's own spreadsheet. Service updates use a template, and once the counselor has written and checked the update, the counselor sends it to the mailing list from the CRM. Visits and personal contact stay with the counselor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each counselor kept their own contact list and sent updates one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared contact lists with mailing are easy to set up.
tasks.human_edge: Earning a school mentor's trust so they call about a student at risk.

evidence.claim: Shared contact lists with mailing can replace personal spreadsheets and one-by-one e-mails.

assumptions: Boundary: from referral sources to the update sent; marketing campaigns are outside.
Input contract: contacts entered by the team; fallback is personal lists.
Visits, personal contact and the check of each update do not change. s3 keeps 50 for adding and updating the counselor's own contacts in the shared list.
Referral sources read updates as they do today; no added time.

incremental.description: No new work: updating contacts after visits is part of s3's remaining time.

approvals.approved_version: The service update exactly as checked by the counselor in s4b, sent once from the CRM to the referral sources' mailing list; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: colleagues do not keep the shared list, so each counselor keeps checking their own, and s3 keeps 80 (8.1); high: a shared list kept by the team (12.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit clients at the workplace, call clients and employers to resolve problems, evaluate placement adequacy, record contacts and agreements, and plan the next visits.

steps.what: Rehabilitation counselor visits clients during job training and placements
Rehabilitation counselor calls clients and employers to resolve problems
Rehabilitation counselor evaluates placement adequacy
Rehabilitation counselor writes contact notes and agreements in the case file
Rehabilitation counselor plans the next visits

tasks.design: The counselor writes contact notes and agreements in the case system ({OTHER}) as today; they are a first record and keep their time. Visits are planned from the case system's due dates into the calendar ({CALENDAR}). Visiting, resolving problems and judging the placement stay with the counselor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed at the end of the day and visits planned by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech-to-text works on phones in Dutch; case systems show due visits.
tasks.still_hard: Problems at the workplace rarely wait for the planned visit.
tasks.human_edge: Settling a clash between a client and a supervisor before it costs the job.

reach.learn: Whether problems are picked up sooner.

evidence.claim: Attendi turns spoken notes into reports in the care record.
Health data are special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the placement to the visits planned; ending the placement is outside.
Input contract: due dates per client in the case system; fallback is the counselor's own list.
Visits, calls and judging the placement do not change.
Clients' and employers' time does not change.
research_questions: Are notes complete on the same day more often?

incremental.description: No new work: due dates already sit in the case system.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: due dates are often missing in the case system, so s5 keeps 85 (0.7); high: visits planned from due dates (2.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The rehabilitation counselor keeps interviewing, assessing, visiting and building trust; typing notes from memory, chasing records and tallying goals shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted notes for invented statements
role.ambitious_version: A counselor with more time for clients at the workplace.
